= Algorithm-engineering checklist for implementation work — 2026-11-05 =

== Public Springer references ==

This checklist is informed by the public publisher pages for the 2016 second
edition of *Encyclopedia of Algorithms* and two entries:

- Springer, [*Encyclopedia of Algorithms*, second edition](https://link.springer.com/referencework/10.1007/978-1-4939-2864-4), DOI `10.1007/978-1-4939-2864-4`.
- [High Performance Algorithm Engineering for Large-Scale Problems](https://link.springer.com/rwe/10.1007/978-1-4939-2864-4_178), DOI `10.1007/978-1-4939-2864-4_178`.
- [Visualization Techniques for Algorithm Engineering](https://link.springer.com/rwe/10.1007/978-1-4939-2864-4_464), DOI `10.1007/978-1-4939-2864-4_464`.

The publisher's overview describes entries that state a problem and its
input/output, summarize results and applications, and point to literature,
open problems, experiments, datasets, and code. Entry `_178` frames algorithm
engineering as turning an abstract method into a robust, efficient,
well-tested, usable implementation, with experimentation central. Entry `_464`
frames the engineering cycle as designing, analyzing, implementing, tuning,
debugging, and experimentally evaluating algorithms; visualization can help
expose practical factors and bottlenecks.

== Practical checklist ==

1. **Write the contract before coding.** Specify accepted input, output,
   encoding, byte/bit order, state initialization, boundaries, version/profile,
   parameters, error behavior, and resource limits. For a packet format, name
   the exact packet tags and versions rather than saying only “PGP” or “AES.”
2. **Trace the mechanics.** Identify each transformation and its ordering from
   source or a specification. A class name, operation title, or search hit is
   not evidence that a complete algorithm is implemented.
3. **Use independent known-answer vectors.** Record the vector's provenance and
   expected output. Prefer a published standard or an independent implementation
   such as GnuPG for interoperability checks; do not validate a port solely
   against outputs generated by the code being ported.
4. **Test both correctness and failure.** Add regression vectors, boundary
   lengths, malformed/truncated inputs, wrong keys/passphrases, tampering, and
   unsupported-version cases. For authenticated formats, assert that altered
   data is rejected and never rendered as successful plaintext.
5. **Duplicate-check before adding a recipe.** Inspect the operation registry,
   recipe packs, and cookbook. Extend a partial operation only when its
   additional behavior and independent vectors are defined; otherwise document
   the exact boundary rather than adding a duplicate or speculative recipe.
6. **Measure only after correctness is pinned down.** Benchmark representative
   inputs, report the environment and workload, and inspect memory, CPU, and
   worst-case behavior. Bound attacker-controlled work factors and input sizes.
7. **Describe the security posture honestly.** Distinguish a format parser from
   a vetted cryptographic library, an integrity check from a digital signature,
   and interoperability evidence from a security audit. Do not promote an
   educational or partial implementation for production use.

== Application to this backlog ==

For OpenPGP work, this means pinning the SKESK and encrypted-data packet versions,
S2K type/hash/count, cipher and mode, integrity/authentication handling, armor
behavior, and unsupported cases. The existing CyberChef classic symmetric
message operation has independent GnuPG control fixtures and negative tests;
that evidence does not automatically validate PGPonyCore's newer packet
profiles or a new browser port. For the Zangi investigation, the observed
Signal-related calls and a separate AES-GCM group-push helper are documented,
but no cellular-automata transform or CA known-answer vector was established.
